s: I'm Maya, and this is my friend Lena.
Today we are talking about travel.
Maya and I both love trips, so this is a fun topic.
And we have five useful travel words for you today.
When you fly somewhere, you go to your gate.
The gate is the place where you get on the plane.
Last summer my gate was number twelve.
I sat at the gate and waited for one hour.
I always check the big screen for my gate.
Sometimes they change the gate, and you have to run!
My gate changed from nine to twenty-five.
I ran across the whole airport to reach the new gate.
Remember, they close the gate about twenty minutes before the flight leaves.
So don't walk away from the gate.
Let's talk about the word depart.
Depart means to leave a place to start a trip.
My morning train departs at eight o'clock.
When a train departs on time, I am so happy.
But buses and trains are not always perfect.
Last week my bus did not depart until ten because of rain.
I check the departures board before I travel.
The board shows when every train departs, so I know what to expect.
And when a flight departs late, you can sit and have coffee.

Arrive means to get to a place at the end of a trip.
I try to arrive early when I fly.
If you arrive late, your gate might close.
I arrived at the hotel at eleven at night once, and the door was locked.
Yes, I called them and they opened the door.
My brother arrived home at midnight after a long flight.
He was so happy to arrive safe and sound.
I love arriving at a new city.
When you arrive, everything feels exciting.
Carry means to hold or take something with you.
Maya, what do you carry when you travel?
I carry one small bag now.
I used to carry three big bags, but that was a mistake!
I carry my passport, my ticket, and my phone.
I also carry snacks, because airport food is too expensive.
My dad carries a huge suitcase everywhere he goes.
I carry only what I really need.
A corner is the place where two streets meet.
Our hotel was on the corner of a busy street.
There was a small cafe on the corner near the train station, and we had breakfast there every day.
If you get lost, ask someone: turn left at the corner.
Last year we met our tour guide at the corner, right next to a flower shop.
Just remember the shop on the corner, and you will find your way back.
Before we say goodbye, one more tip.

Let's say our five words one more time.
Gate — the place where you get on the plane.
Depart — to leave to start a trip.
Arrive — to get to a place.
Carry — to take things with you.
Use them this week when you talk about travel.
Thanks for listening to Muse English.
